title: Multi-vendor label feed: validate, merge, summarise
scenario: Three vendors deliver sentiment labels as a BOM-prefixed CSV, a plain CSV and JSON. Rows are validated, copies of the same task are merged (latest wins, ties go to the most trusted vendor, tags unioned), and Test 3 summarises labels, tags and batches.

verified.why_correct: The `%d.%m.%Y` format looks like it swaps day and month compared with the slash format, but the README says dotted dates are day.month.year and slash dates are month/day/year. Returning None for unparseable values is intentional: validation turns None into bad_timestamp.

bugs.title: Zero duration treated as missing
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_rejections: an extra entry acme:3 -> [missing_duration] (T003 from acme has duration 0). Records are unchanged because cortex wins T003 anyway.
bugs.why: `not rec.duration_s` is True for 0 as well as None, so a real zero-second duration is rejected. The README says 0 is a real value.
hints: Look at acme row 3 in the data. Which rule could reject it?
Check how validate.py decides a duration is missing.
`if not rec.duration_s` also catches 0. Use `if rec.duration_s is None`.
probes: Why did the T003 record not change even though one of its copies was rejected?
Which other values would `not x` treat as missing that a `None` check would not?

bugs.title: Equal-time tie goes to the least trusted vendor
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_same_time_submissions: T008 goes to brightlabel (k.osei) and T015 to cortex (s.ito). They should be acme and brightlabel.
bugs.why: merge() takes max() of rank, so the tie-break term must grow as trust grows. Priority 1 is the most trusted, so it has to be negated; without the minus the largest priority number (least trusted) wins.
hints: T008 was submitted by acme and brightlabel at the same minute. Which vendor should win per the README?
Look at the key merge() uses to pick the winning copy.
rank returns (submitted, priority); it should be (submitted, -priority).
probes: Why does the comment in rank() not help you here?
If two copies from the same vendor had the same timestamp, which would win and why?

bugs.title: Merged tags not de-duplicated
bugs.old: tags = sorted({tag for rec in copies for tag in rec.tags})
bugs.new: tags = sorted(tag for rec in copies for tag in rec.tags)
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_merged_tags: merged records repeat tags, e.g. T001 [sentiment, sentiment, short, short], T002 [sarcasm, sentiment, sentiment].
bugs.why: Without the set, a tag that appears on several copies is repeated in the final record. The README says the tags are the sorted distinct tags.
hints: T001 has 'sentiment' twice. Where are tags from the copies combined?
Sort a set comprehension, not a generator: sorted({tag for ...}).
probes: Why did tag_counts in the summary stay correct while this was present?
Why didn't single-copy records show repeated tags?

bugs.title: Vendor label maps share one dict
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_label_counts: {negative: 7, neutral: 7, positive: 8}; the mixed: 1 entry is gone and neutral is one too high.
bugs.why: A shallow copy shares the nested `label_map` dict, so each vendor's update() writes into the defaults and every vendor ends up using the union of all maps. brightlabel's `mixed → neutral` leaks into cortex.
hints: T024 came from cortex with label 'mixed'. Does cortex's label_map mention 'mixed'?
Look at how each vendor's settings are built from the defaults in config.py.
copy.copy shares label_map between vendors; use copy.deepcopy(defaults).
probes: Why didn't the priorities leak between vendors the same way?
Would `dict(defaults)` have fixed it? Why or why not?

bugs.title: Removing tags from the list being iterated
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_tag_counts: an extra tmp:review: 1 entry.
bugs.why: Removing an element shifts the rest left, so the loop skips the element after each removal. In 'tmp:qa;tmp:review;short' the second internal tag is never checked and survives.
hints: Where does 'tmp:review' come from, and why wasn't 'tmp:qa' left in too?
Look at the loop in split_tags that drops blank and internal tags.
Iterate over a copy (`for tag in list(tags):`) or build a new list with a comprehension.
probes: Why were single tmp: tags (T018, T029) removed correctly?
Why didn't this show up in any record test?

bugs.title: BOM kept in the first CSV header
bugs.old: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
bugs.new: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_by_batch: {b1: 2, b4: 4, b5: 3, b6: 5, unbatched: 8}; b2 and b3 vanish and every acme winner lands in unbatched.
bugs.why: acme.csv starts with a byte order mark. Read as plain utf-8, the first header becomes '\ufeffbatch', so raw.get('batch') is None for every acme row and they all fall back to 'unbatched'.
hints: Every acme winner is in 'unbatched'. Print the keys of one acme row.
Look at how CSV files are opened in loader.py.
Open CSVs with encoding="utf-8-sig" so the BOM is stripped.
probes: Why did only the batch field break, and not task_id or email?
Why did brightlabel.csv load fine with the same code?

context_qa.q: What is the flow inside build_report()?
context_qa.a: It resolves vendor settings from vendors.json, then for each vendor (sorted) loads its file with `load_vendor`, records the row count, and splits rows with `validate.partition`. All accepted rows go to `dedupe.dedupe`, which returns one record per task id, and `summarize` builds the summary from those records.

context_qa.q: How are vendor settings built from the defaults?
context_qa.a: `config.vendor_settings` loops over the vendor names, copies `defaults`, calls `update()` on the copy's `label_map` with the vendor's own map, then sets every other key from the vendor entry. The result is keyed by the trimmed, lower-cased name.

context_qa.q: What does read_rows return for a CSV vs. the JSON file?
context_qa.a: For `.json` it returns the parsed list of objects. For anything else it returns `list(csv.DictReader(fh))`, so a list of dicts keyed by the header names as they appear in the file.

context_qa.q: What does split_tags do with a list vs. a string?
context_qa.a: A list is used as is; a string is trimmed and split on ';'. Each part is trimmed and lower-cased, then a loop removes blank entries and entries starting with `tmp:` from that list.

context_qa.q: How does merge() pick the winning copy?
context_qa.a: `max(copies, key=rank)`, where `rank` returns a tuple built from `submitted` and the copy's `priority`. max() keeps the first copy if two have equal keys, and copies are in load order (vendor name, then file order).
For each final record it counts each tag once (it iterates over `set(rec.tags)`), so the value is the number of final records carrying the tag.

context_qa.q: Where does the row number in a rejection key come from?
context_qa.a: `load_vendor` enumerates the rows from 1 and stores the index in `Record.row`; `Rejection.key` formats it as `vendor:row`.
